memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Abraham rose and bowed down before the people of the land, the Hittites. He said to them, "If you are willing to let me bury my dead, then listen to me and intercede with Ephron son of Zohar on my behalf so he will sell me the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to him and is at the end of his field..." - Gen 23:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even in his grief, Abraham is gracious and courteous. He rises, bows respectfully before the people, and makes his request with humility and honour. He does not use his sorrow as an excuse for rudeness, nor his standing as a "mighty prince" to demand what he wants. He asks politely, treating others with dignity even in his time of pain.

This is a beautiful and challenging example. Grief can make us short-tempered, self-absorbed, careless of others. When we are hurting, we often excuse ourselves from kindness. But Abraham, in the depths of loss, still honours those around him. His faith shaped his conduct even when his heart was breaking.

There is real godliness in this. How we treat others in our hardest moments reveals what is truly in us. It is easy to be gracious when life is smooth; it is a mark of deep character to remain kind, courteous, and considerate when we are suffering.

Notice too that Abraham wanted to do things rightly and honourably - asking to purchase the cave, not simply take it. Integrity and courtesy marked even his grief. This reflects the character God calls us to: to "be completely humble and gentle" (Eph 4:2), and to let our "gentleness be evident to all" (Phil 4:5). When you are hurting, ask God to help you still honour others. Grief is no excuse to abandon grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does your grief or pain ever become an excuse to treat others poorly?
- How can you show grace and courtesy even in hard times?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when I am hurting, keep me from using my pain as an excuse to be unkind. Help me honour others with grace and courtesy even in my hardest moments, so that my conduct reflects You.
Amen.
